memoryText: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read 1 John 1:9 slowly, several times, and try to say it from memory. Then read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
This verse is a gift for anyone who has failed. The condition is simple: confess. To confess means to say the same thing about our sin that God says, not minimizing, excusing, or blaming. We do not have to clean ourselves up first.

The promise is two-sided. God is faithful: he keeps his covenant promises. And he is just: the penalty has been paid by Christ, so God does not forgive by ignoring justice but by satisfying it. Therefore the forgiveness is certain.

The result has two parts: forgiveness of our sins (the guilt is removed) and cleansing from unrighteousness (the stain and power of sin are dealt with). We are not left in the pit.

When shame tells you to hide, say this verse to God, and then name the specific sin. Accept his forgiveness, and walk in the light.
weekInReview: This week you read Psalms 118 and 31, all of 1 John, and a pause on perseverance. Psalm 118 told us to give thanks to the LORD, whose steadfast love endures forever, and to take refuge in him rather than in man. Psalm 31 gave the prayer of committing our spirit into God’s hand. First John 1 and 2 taught us that God is light, that confession brings forgiveness, that Christ is our advocate and propitiation, and that we must not love the world. First John 3 marveled at the love of the Father who calls us his children, and defined love as laying down our lives in deed and truth. First John 4 and 5 taught us to test the spirits, that God is love, that perfect love casts out fear, and that we can know that we have eternal life. Day 860 was a pause on perseverance and assurance: God keeps his people, and he wants us to know it.
reflectionQuestions: John gives several tests of genuine faith: believing that Jesus came in the flesh, obeying God’s commands, and loving one another. Which of these tests encourages you most, and which do you want to grow in?
John says Jesus Christ the righteous is our advocate with the Father and the propitiation for our sins. How does knowing that Christ pleads for you change the way you respond when you sin?
John writes that he wants you to know you have eternal life. What gives you confidence about your salvation, and what makes you doubt? What promise of Scripture can you hold on to this week?
prayerPrompts: Confess your sins to God, naming them without excuse.
Thank him that he is faithful and just to forgive and cleanse.
